Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G251; saltless, i.e. insipid:--X lose saltness.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in Jesus' saying about salt: salt is good, but if it has lost its saltness, nothing can season it again — so have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another. It is salt without saltiness — the thing that has lost the very quality that made it useful, and cannot get it back.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for saltless carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the question — salt that has lost its saltness, and what it is good for then.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
